title: Confirming Claims of Superposition and Adversarial Examples in Toy Models
primary_claim: This work replicates all three core claims of Stevinson et al. (arXiv:2510.11709) in toy superposition classifiers: PGD adversarial attacks align with the theoretically optimal interference-exploiting perturbation, robustness falls monotonically as superposition (k/m) increases and rises to 97.3% when k=m, and adversarial attacks transfer between independently-trained models in proportion to how much their feature geometries converge under correlated input regimes; it additionally finds that co-activating features can collapse onto a shared direction rather than orthogonalizing when bottleneck capacity is limited.
quote: We reproduce all three core claims of Stevinson et al. from their toy classifier setting
metric: PGD-attack vs optimal-perturbation cosine similarity; robust accuracy vs k/m
target_value: PGD·optimal cosine similarity = 1.00 across tested k/m (vs paper's 0.92-0.97); robust accuracy at k=m rises to 97.3% (m=5), falling monotonically as k/m increases (e.g. k/m=4, m=5: 30.1% ours vs 33.5% paper)
tolerance_rationale: headline is a compound of 9 numbers; compare the components by hand
inspector_notes: Fully self-contained toy replication with one CLI entrypoint that runs every sub-experiment and builds the comparison report; the repo's own README already documents an instability in the paper's own H3 seed-sampling result (N=10 seeds) as a finding, not a repro blocker.
headline_artifact: results/h1_alignment.json (PGD-vs-optimal cosine similarity), results/h2_control.json (robust accuracy vs k/m), results/h3_transfer.json (geometry-transfer correlation), assembled into report.html

extension.what_varies: a plain venv (torch/numpy/matplotlib) resolved with --exclude-newer 2026-08-15 (post 2026-08-01 + 14 d), outside the queue's tree_prep. Code, data, target unchanged.
extension.rationale: parent ledgered env ('prep returns nonzero in-queue, 4 attempts; run never reached') -- a harness-side failure, not a repo failure. Post-date environment == today's environment, so this is the cleanest 'rotten at publication' test in the series; if it runs, the 'env' label was the harness's.
